title: Master list of official verified trusted sources
method: Each entry was verified line-by-line during the 2026-09-18 or 2026-09-19 sessions: the URL was fetched directly, or located via live search when a direct fetch failed (noted per entry, with status verified-via-search), and the 'verified' field records exactly what was observed on the official source. Nothing in this list is assumed. 32 entries (2026-09-18) + 21 entries (2026-09-19) + 20 entries (2026-09-19 second batch: academic pollsters, race raters, campaign-finance, official election-administration and research layers; iem entry URL-corrected in the same batch) = 73.

sources.name: Kalshi (exchange, API & docs)
sources.type: Official exchange (CFTC-licensed DCM) + market data layer
sources.verified: Live public API queried 2026-09-18: GET /series, GET /markets (series_ticker filters PRES, CONTROLH, CONTROLS, SENATEAZ), GET /historical/cutoff, GET /historical/markets (settled 2024 markets with result=yes/no), GET /markets/{t}/candlesticks (daily history). Historical data docs page fetched: market_settled_ts partitioning confirmed.
sources.notes: Primary prediction-market data layer for this project.

sources.name: Federal Election Commission — Election Results
sources.type: Official government (results compiled from state election offices)
sources.verified: FEC page fetched via search (2026-09-18): 'Official 2024 Presidential General Election Results, compiled from state election offices (PDF)'; biennial 'Federal Elections' compilations described. 2024 results PDF cited by Wikipedia infobox: https://www.fec.gov/resources/cms-content/documents/2024presgeresults.pdf
sources.notes: Authoritative source for certified federal results (2020: 81,283,501 Biden / 74,223,975 Trump; 2024: 77,302,580 Trump / 75,017,613 Harris per the FEC PDF via Wikipedia infobox).

sources.name: U.S. Election Assistance Commission (EAC)
sources.verified: Verified via usa.gov agency page + Ballotpedia/Wikipedia (2026-09-18): federal commission created by HAVA 2002; develops voting system guidelines/certification.
sources.notes: FLAGGED: as of July 2026 the commission has no serving commissioners (two dismissed, one resigned) — irregularity #1; treat its guidance output accordingly until reconstituted.

sources.verified: Census press release (2023-05-02) fetched via search: 2022 turnout 52.2% of CVAP, registration 69.1%; NBER-hosted raw files with DOI 10.60592/w6zf-md62 also located.
sources.notes: 2024 presidential turnout 64.3% (per University of Florida, cited in Wikipedia infobox) and 2020 turnout 66.6% (U.S. Elections Project, same infobox) — Census CPS is the comparable series.

sources.name: Roper Center for Public Opinion Research (Cornell University)
sources.type: Academic public-opinion data archive (first social-science data archive, 1947)
sources.verified: Directly fetched 2026-09-19: mission 'to collect, preserve, and disseminate public opinion data'; founded from Elmo Roper's 1947 donation (Fortune Survey 1935-1950 — first scientific national poll; correct 1936 FDR landslide call); iPoll question/dataset search; publicly accessible Presidential approval ratings application (cross-president comparison); 'one of the few places that makes available state and national exit polls, back to 1972'; 'Dive Into Elections and Presidents' data-highlight collection; free classroom materials; 2026 Mitofsky Award to Scott Keeter (Pew).
sources.notes: CRITICAL for the exit-poll backtest layer: state + national exit polls 1972-present and 50+ years of presidential approval — the historical poll archive the project's poll archive (which currently ends 2024-09-12) can be extended against. Free registration for iPoll.
